title: 春よ、来い (Haru yo, Koi — Come, Spring)
description:
A sweeping ballad by 松任谷由実 (Matsutoya Yumi, known as Yuming), released on October 24, 1994 as her 26th single. It was written as the theme song for the NHK morning drama (朝ドラ)『春よ、来い』of the same year. The song is a meditation on longing — spring is both the season and a metaphor for a beloved person or a lost time in one's life that the narrator waits to return.

The imagery is strikingly classical: 沈丁花 (daphne flower, a fragrant early-spring plant), 俄雨 (sudden shower), and 淡き光 (pale/dim light) evoke waka poetry traditions. The line 流るる雨のごとく / 流るる花のごとく uses the archaic verb form 流るる (classical continuative form of 流れる) — a deliberate literary register shift. The song sold over 1.16 million copies, making it one of Yuming's best-selling singles.

For learners: Solidly N2 due to classical grammar and literary vocabulary. Key points: 淡き (classical adjective form; modern would be 淡い), 俄雨 (にわかあめ — sudden/passing shower; 俄 is an N2 kanji meaning 'sudden'), 沈丁花 (じんちょうげ — daphne; a flower name learners rarely encounter), 面影 (おもかげ — memory of a face / image of someone; literary N2 word), 瞼 (まぶた — eyelid; N2 kanji), 流るる (classical attributive form of 流れる — used for poetic effect), ごとく (classical 'like/as' — equivalent to modern ように), 眼差し (まなざし — gaze / look in one's eyes; N2 literary word). The sustained use of classical forms and the density of literary vocabulary place this firmly at N2.
